Relations between groups of triangles

Source: R/tri_ops.R
tri_relate.Rd

The DE-9IM matrix (as ST_Relate() returns it) between pairs of groups of one triangle mesh, computed from shared triangles, edges and vertices alone, without reading coordinates.

Usage

tri_relate(x, group = NULL, pairs = NULL)

Arguments

x

A wkpool_tri.

group

Groups of triangles. Either one integer per triangle (a dense, 1-based group id, NA to leave a triangle out), or a data frame with columns triangle (row in x) and group, for groups that overlap (a triangle in several groups, as in an overlay). The default is the triangles' feature, or one group when the pool has no feature.

pairs

NULL for every pair of groups that share a vertex (all pairs that are not disjoint), or a two-column matrix or data frame of group ids.

Value

A data frame with columns a, b (group ids) and relate (the nine-character DE-9IM string, interior, boundary, exterior of a by those of b).

Details

Every point of the plane lies in exactly one open triangle, open edge or vertex of the mesh, or outside it, and each of those lies wholly in the interior, boundary or exterior of a group. A triangle is interior when it is in the group. An edge is interior when the triangles on both sides are, boundary when one is (outside the mesh is never in a group). A vertex is interior when every triangle around it is in the group and it is not on the outside of the mesh, exterior when none is, and boundary otherwise. Each matrix entry is the largest dimension of a mesh element in both classes: "2" for a triangle, "1" for an edge, "0" for a vertex, "F" for none.

The answer is exact for the mesh as given. It equals the relation of the polygons the groups cover when the mesh was built so that every place two inputs meet is a shared vertex, as a constrained triangulation that resolves crossings does. Pairs of groups that share no vertex are disjoint, "FF2FF1212", and are not listed when pairs is NULL.

Examples

## a 2 x 1 strip of unit squares and a group covering both
v <- data.frame(.vx = 1:6, x = c(0, 1, 1, 0, 2, 2), y = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1))
tri <- new_wkpool_tri(v, vx0 = c(1, 1, 2, 2), vx1 = c(2, 3, 5, 6),
                      vx2 = c(3, 4, 6, 3))
g <- data.frame(triangle = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4),
                group = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3))
tri_relate(tri, g)
#>   a b    relate
#> 1 1 2 FF2F11212
#> 2 1 3 2FF11F212
#> 3 2 3 2FF11F212
